passages.text: This is the burden against Damascus: “Behold, Damascus is no longer a city; it has become a heap of ruins.
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave a message about Damascus.
Damascus was once a city.
Now Damascus is no longer a city.
Damascus has become a heap of ruins.
passages.original: מַשָּׂ֖א דַּמָּ֑שֶׂק הִנֵּ֤ה דַמֶּ֙שֶׂק֙ מוּסָ֣ר מֵעִ֔יר וְהָיְתָ֖ה מְעִ֥י מַפָּלָֽה׃

passages.text: The cities of Aroer are forsaken; they will be left to the flocks, which will lie down with no one to fear.
passages.sermon:
The cities of Aroer are empty.
No people live there.
Flocks will live in these cities.
The flocks will lie down in peace.
No one will make them afraid.
passages.original: עֲזֻב֖וֹת עָרֵ֣י עֲרֹעֵ֑ר לַעֲדָרִ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ינָה וְרָבְצ֖וּ וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃

passages.text: The fortress will disappear from Ephraim, and the sovereignty from Damascus. The remnant of Aram will be like the splendor of the Israelites,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He declares what will happen.
Ephraim is a tribe of Israel.
Damascus is a great city.
Aram is a nation near Israel.
The fortress will disappear from Ephraim.
Damascus will lose its kingdom.
Only a remnant will remain in Aram.
This remnant will be like the splendor of the Israelites.
passages.original: וְנִשְׁבַּ֤ת מִבְצָר֙ מֵֽאֶפְרַ֔יִם וּמַמְלָכָ֥ה מִדַּמֶּ֖שֶׂק וּשְׁאָ֣ר אֲרָ֑ם כִּכְב֤וֹד בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יִֽהְי֔וּ נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: “In that day the splendor of Jacob will fade, and the fat of his body will waste away, as the reaper gathers the standing grain and harvests the ears with his arm, as one gleans heads of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the ancestor of the Israelites.
God spoke about a future day.
On that day, Jacob’s splendor will fade.
His strength and glory will become weak.
His body will lose its fat.
He will become thin and wasted.
This will happen like a reaper gathers standing grain.
The reaper uses his arm to cut the ears of grain.
It will also be like someone gleaning heads of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
Only a few heads of grain will remain.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִדַּ֖ל כְּב֣וֹד יַעֲקֹ֑ב וּמִשְׁמַ֥ן בְּשָׂר֖וֹ יֵרָזֶֽה׃ וְהָיָ֗ה כֶּֽאֱסֹף֙ קָצִ֣יר קָמָ֔ה וּזְרֹע֖וֹ שִׁבֳּלִ֣ים יִקְצ֑וֹר וְהָיָ֛ה כִּמְלַקֵּ֥ט שִׁבֳּלִ֖ים בְּעֵ֥מֶק רְפָאִֽים׃

passages.text: Yet gleanings will remain, like an olive tree that has been beaten— two or three berries atop the tree, four or five on its fruitful branches,” declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD declares this message.
Some people will remain.
They will be like leftover fruit after an olive tree is beaten.
Two or three berries will stay at the top of the tree.
Four or five berries will remain on its fruitful branches.
passages.original: וְנִשְׁאַר־ בּ֤וֹ עֽוֹלֵלֹת֙ כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת שְׁנַ֧יִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֛ה גַּרְגְּרִ֖ים בְּרֹ֣אשׁ אָמִ֑יר אַרְבָּעָ֣ה חֲמִשָּׁ֗ה בִּסְעִפֶ֙יהָ֙ פֹּֽרִיָּ֔ה נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: In that day men will look to their Maker and turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel.
passages.sermon: On that day, people will look to their Maker.\r\nThey will turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִשְׁעֶ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם עַל־ עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ וְעֵינָ֕יו אֶל־ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּרְאֶֽינָה׃

passages.text: They will not look to the altars they have fashioned with their hands or to the Asherahs and incense altars they have made with their fingers.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD, the God of Israel.
God speaks about the people of Israel.
The people once made altars with their own hands.
They also made Asherah poles and incense altars with their fingers.
In that day, the people will not look at these altars.
They will not see the Asherah poles or the incense altars they made.
passages.original: וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁעֶ֔ה אֶל־ הַֽמִּזְבְּח֖וֹת מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדָ֑יו וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֤וּ אֶצְבְּעֹתָיו֙ לֹ֣א יִרְאֶ֔ה וְהָאֲשֵׁרִ֖ים וְהָחַמָּנִֽים׃

passages.text: In that day their strong cities will be like forsaken thickets and summits, abandoned to the Israelites and to utter desolation.
passages.sermon:
On that day, God will act in judgment.
The people’s strong cities will become weak.
These cities will be like thickets that no one cares for.
They will be like hilltops that people have left behind.
Long ago, the Israelites abandoned such places.
Now, these cities will be empty.
They will become completely desolate.
passages.original: בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא יִהְי֣וּ׀ עָרֵ֣י מָעֻזּ֗וֹ כַּעֲזוּבַ֤ת הַחֹ֙רֶשׁ֙ וְהָ֣אָמִ֔יר אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָזְב֔וּ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהָיְתָ֖ה שְׁמָמָֽה׃

passages.text: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and failed to remember the Rock of your refuge. Therefore, though you cultivate delightful plots and set out cuttings from exotic vines— though on the day you plant you make them grow, and on that morning you help your seed sprout— yet the harvest will vanish on the day of disease and incurable pain.
passages.sermon:
You have forgotten God.
God is the one who saves you.
You did not remember the Rock.
The Rock is your place of safety.
Because of this, you plant pleasant gardens.
You plant foreign vines.
You make your plants grow on the day you plant them.
You help your seeds sprout in the morning.
But the harvest will disappear.
This will happen on a day of sickness.
This will happen when pain cannot be healed.
passages.original: כִּ֤י שָׁכַ֙חַתְּ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעֵ֔ךְ וְצ֥וּר מָעֻזֵּ֖ךְ לֹ֣א זָכָ֑רְתְּ עַל־ כֵּ֗ן תִּטְּעִי֙ נִטְעֵ֣י נַעֲמָנִ֔ים וּזְמֹ֥רַת זָ֖ר תִּזְרָעֶֽנּוּ׃ בְּי֤וֹם נִטְעֵךְ֙ תְּשַׂגְשֵׂ֔גִי וּבַבֹּ֖קֶר זַרְעֵ֣ךְ תַּפְרִ֑יחִי נֵ֥ד קָצִ֛יר בְּי֥וֹם נַחֲלָ֖ה וּכְאֵ֥ב אָנֽוּשׁ׃ס

passages.text: Alas, the tumult of many peoples; they rage like the roaring seas and clamoring nations; they rumble like the crashing of mighty waters.
passages.sermon:
Many peoples gather together.
They make a loud noise.
They roar like the sea.
Many nations shout.
They sound like mighty waters crashing.
passages.original: ה֗וֹי הֲמוֹן֙ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים כַּהֲמ֥וֹת יַמִּ֖ים יֶהֱמָי֑וּן וּשְׁא֣וֹן לְאֻמִּ֔ים כִּשְׁא֛וֹן מַ֥יִם כַּבִּירִ֖ים יִשָּׁאֽוּן׃

passages.text: The nations rage like the rush of many waters. He rebukes them, and they flee far away, driven before the wind like chaff on the hills, like tumbleweeds before a gale.
passages.sermon:
The nations are many.
The nations make a loud noise.
Their noise is like the sound of rushing waters.
God rebukes the nations.
The nations flee far away.
The wind drives them away.
They are like chaff on the hills before the wind.
They are like tumbleweeds before a strong storm.
passages.original: לְאֻמִּ֗ים כִּשְׁא֞וֹן מַ֤יִם רַבִּים֙ יִשָּׁא֔וּן וְגָ֥עַר בּ֖וֹ וְנָ֣ס מִמֶּרְחָ֑ק וְרֻדַּ֗ף כְּמֹ֤ץ הָרִים֙ לִפְנֵי־ ר֔וּחַ וּכְגַלְגַּ֖ל לִפְנֵ֥י סוּפָֽה׃

passages.text: In the evening, there is sudden terror! Before morning, they are no more! This is the portion of those who loot us and the lot of those who plunder us.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about those who attack His people.
In the evening, terror comes suddenly.
Before morning, the attackers are gone.
God removes them quickly.
This is the fate of those who loot us.
This is the destiny of those who plunder us.
passages.original: לְעֵ֥ת עֶ֙רֶב֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה בַלָּהָ֔ה בְּטֶ֥רֶם בֹּ֖קֶר אֵינֶ֑נּוּ זֶ֚ה חֵ֣לֶק שׁוֹסֵ֔ינוּ וְגוֹרָ֖ל לְבֹזְזֵֽינוּ׃ס
